Enjoy a high-speed gaming experience and work efficiency with the Lexar ® NM760 M.2 2280 PCIe Gen4x4 NVMe SSD. Designed for gamers and professionals with speeds of up to 5300MB/s read and 4500MB/s 1 write, get 9.6x 3 the performance compared to traditional SATA-based SSD. Enjoy the coolness. With an optional heatsink, you can unleash the outstanding performance and don’t need to worry about sudden performance drops from high temperature.

Built to Last. Unlike traditional hard disk drives, the NM760 SSD has no moving parts, so it’s built to last. On top of that, it’s also shock and vibration resistant 2, making it one robust and reliable SSD.

Widely compatible with various devices. The NM760 is widely compatible with notebooks, PC, PlayStation ® 5 and etc., delivers powerful performance for high-speed storage backup and access to content

Title: Lexar NM760 M.2 PCIe Gen4 NVMe SSD Review : Quite pricey
URL: https://www.digit.in/reviews/general/lexar-nm760-m-2-2280-pcie-gen4-nvme-ssd-review-346929.html
Published: 2023-05-26T15:17:00.000Z
Author: Mithun Mohandas
Highlights:
## Lexar NM760 NVMe SSD Specifications

The Lexar NM760 is a mid-tier NVMe 1.4 SSD. Mid-tier because it does support really high transfer speeds thanks to the Silicon Motion SM2269 controller but because it is DRAM-less, there will be performance drops across sustained workloads. As per the specifications, the Lexar NM760 1 TB SKU claims to have sequential read speeds of up to 5300 MBps and write speeds of up to 4500 MBps. As for IOPS, it is rated for 440K for read and 900K for write operations. Lexar provides a 5-year warranty for the NM760 with an MTBF i.e. Mean Time Before Failure of 1.5 million operating hours.

...

The controller on the NM760 is a Silicon Motion SM2269XTF which is a popular choice for SSDs without a DRAM cache. It is a 4 Channel PCIe Gen 4.0 controller with x4 PCIe lanes and support for NVMe 1.4 protocol. It’s built using the TSMC 12nm process node so the power savings should be significant. The peak transfer speeds supported by the SM2269 family is 5100 MB/s as per Silicon Motion’s own data sheet but in our tests, it does cross that threshold quite often.

Coming to the NAND, the NM760 has two Longsys RC72TAA1442512G which are 512 GB B47R chips manufactured by Micron. Lexar was owned by Micron and the brand was purchased by Longsys in 2017 so most of the parts will all be Micron.
